paper: Pinelis (2006) Student's t-test without symmetry conditions
what_it_proves: Mixture of two-point zero-mean laws; exact conservative inequalities for asymmetry-corrected self-normalized sums, independent summands (no finite-pop, no max-share class)

paper: Efron (1969) Student's t-test under symmetry conditions, JASA 64
what_it_proves: Self-normalized sum under orthant symmetry: P(S>=x)<=exp(-x^2/2); T monotone in S. Not re-read; via Pinelis citation

paper: Pinelis (1994) / Eaton (1970,74) / Edelman (1990)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701806 (Pinelis); Edelman 1990 cited in Romano 2004 refs, not fetched
what_it_proves: Sharp Khinchin/Rademacher tail bounds -> t-test conservative under symmetry; exact extremal weighted Rademacher (k-sparse) problem

paper: Pinelis (2015) On the supremum of the tails of normalized sums of independent Rademacher r.v.s, SPL 99
what_it_proves: Maximal tail M(x)=sup over unit l2 weights; disproves conjecture that equal-weight is extremal

paper: Edelman (2025) Worst-case Nonparametric Bounds for the Student T-statistic
what_it_proves: Claims k-sparse equal-weight maximisers for weighted Rademacher sums; main result refuted by Pinelis comment arXiv:2509.02410

paper: Pinelis (2025) Comment on Edelman
what_it_proves: Shows Edelman's Theorem 1 false

paper: Lehmann & Loh (1990) Pointwise vs uniform robustness, Scand J Stat 17
what_it_proves: Asymptotic: t-test not uniformly robust over KS nbhd or bounded-support classes; uniformly robust if standardized moments uniformly bounded
contains_K_K2: partly (asymptotic uniformity, no finite-sample critical values)

paper: Chen & Loh (1990) Uniform robustness against nonnormality of t and F tests, CommStat-TM 19
what_it_proves: Size of t test can be 1 over arbitrary dists; controlling tail-heaviness restores uniform size control (asymptotic)

paper: Romano (2004) On non-parametric testing, uniform behaviour of the t-test, Scand J Stat 31
what_it_proves: Size of t-test is 1 for most nonparametric models; uniform asymptotic validity under uniform integrability of standardized variable; asymptotic maximin optimality

paper: Romano & Wolf (2000) Finite sample nonparametric inference and large sample efficiency, AoS 28
what_it_proves: Finite-sample conservative CIs for mean on known compact support; bounded support, not scale-free t

paper: Bahadur & Savage (1956); Gleser & Hwang (1987); Dufour (1997)
what_it_proves: Impossibility of effective CIs for mean without restrictions (background knowledge; not re-verified)

paper: Bakirov & Szekely (2006) Student's t-test for Gaussian scale mixtures
what_it_proves: t-test conservative at level <=~8.3% under independent Gaussian heterogeneous variances; Ibragimov-Muller 2010 builds on it
contains_K_K2: partly (K2 flavour: few heterogeneous clusters; Gaussian, not max-share class)

paper: Ibragimov & Muller (2010) t-statistic based correlation and heterogeneity robust inference, JBES 28
what_it_proves: t-test on q group estimates, conservative for heterogeneous Gaussian variances; asymptotic validity

paper: Hendriks, IJzerman-Boon, Klaassen (2006) Student's t-statistic under unimodal densities, Austrian J Stat 35
what_it_proves: Extremal (uniform) parent for t quantiles in symmetric unimodal iid class

paper: Sugden, Smith, Jones (2000) Cochran's rule for SRS, JRSS B 62
what_it_proves: Edgeworth-based minimum n (n>28+25 g1^2) for SRSWOR Studentized mean; asymptotic, skewness-based

paper: Qing & Valliant (2025) Extending Cochran's rule to stratified SRS, J Off Stat
what_it_proves: Edgeworth-based per-stratum minimum n; asymptotic; K2-adjacent heuristics

paper: Bloznelis (1999) Berry-Esseen bound for finite population Student's statistic, AoP 27
what_it_proves: Berry-Esseen for Studentized mean under SRSWOR, minimal conditions; non-sharp constants, not a certified coverage/critical value

paper: Bentkus-Gotze (1996); Bentkus-Bloznelis-Gotze (1996)
what_it_proves: Berry-Esseen for Student statistic iid / non-iid (Lindeberg-type)

paper: Hu, Robinson, Wang (2007) Cramer-type large deviations for samples from a finite population, AoS
what_it_proves: Cramer-type large deviations incl. finite-population Student t; asymptotic

paper: Giné-Götze-Mason (1997); Hajek (1960); Logan-Mallows-Rice-Shepp (1973)
what_it_proves: CLT for Studentized sums / finite population Lindeberg-Hajek condition (max-share -> 0 flavour); background knowledge

paper: Waudby-Smith & Ramdas (2024) Estimating means of bounded r.v.s by betting, JRSS B 86
what_it_proves: Finite-sample CIs for bounded means incl. WoR; needs known bounded range, not scale-free

paper: Serfling (1974) / Bardenet-Maillard (2015) / Hoeffding (1963)
what_it_proves: WoR concentration bounds for bounded variables; known range required

paper: Pinelis (2015) Optimal binomial/Poisson/normal left-tail domination for nonnegative sums
what_it_proves: Exact bounds on E f(S_n) for nonnegative independent summands given first two moments

paper: 'The Exact Worst-Case Tail Probability under Bounded Kurtosis' (arXiv 2026; authors not checked)
what_it_proves: Exact sup_{kurtosis<=kappa} P(X>=t) for a single variable (population tails, not t statistic)

paper: Phan, Thomas, Ramdas; Shekhar & Ramdas
what_it_proves: Betting/e-value finite-population & bounded-support intervals; not individually searched (background knowledge)

paper: Kim (2003) Finite-sample distributions of self-normalized sums, Bundesbank DP
what_it_proves: Simulated quantiles of Student t under stable laws; no guarantees

paper: Stratified Permutational Berry-Esseen bounds (2025)
what_it_proves: Stein-method BE bounds for stratified permutation statistics, heterogeneous strata; asymptotic bounds

paper: Potscher & Preinerstorfer (2024) size controllability of heteroskedasticity-robust tests
what_it_proves: Gaussian linear-model size controllability, few clusters; (already known to project)
